items.fix:
Give the audio its own section, e.g. `

Listen to this release

`, holding the player and transcript link. Name the control by its action: "Play audio briefing, synthetic voice, about 25 seconds". Test with NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver heading navigation.
items.impact: The alternative format is easy to miss for the users most likely to want it (screen-reader users, users with cognitive disabilities who scan headings), and pressing the button starts speech without warning.
items.problem: The audio control and its transcript link sit in a bare paragraph with no heading or landmark. A screen-reader user moving by headings goes from "At a glance" straight to "Main points" and never learns an audio briefing exists. The button name "Audio briefing (1 minute)" names a thing, not an action, so it does not say pressing it starts sound. Evidence: the paragraph's position in the markup and the button text.
items.where:
bulletin.html, `

Audio briefing script

`, between the "At a glance" section and `

Main points

`

items.fix: Use a native `<audio controls preload="none">` with `<source src="audio-briefing.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">` and a fallback download link inside. Add a visible "Download audio (MP3, 0.4 MB)" link next to the transcript link. Offer playback-speed control in any custom player. Test with JavaScript disabled, in reader mode, and with users who change speed.
items.impact: Some users meet a control that does nothing and do not know why. Others, such as blind or partially sighted users, people with dyslexia, and people with cognitive or processing disabilities, cannot replay the audio at a speed they can follow or keep it to listen again.
items.problem: The button is in static HTML but only works through `new Audio('audio-briefing.mp3').play()`. If the script fails, is blocked, or runs in reader mode or a simplified browser, the button does nothing. No link to the MP3 is given, so users cannot open it in their own player, and the `Audio` object offers no playback-rate control. Evidence: the script is the only place the MP3 is referenced, and the button has no fallback.
items.where: bulletin.html, the `<button id="audio">` and the `<script>` block; the only reference to `audio-briefing.mp3` is inside the script

items.fix: Put the "Official statistics" designation on the human-checked content, such as the "Main points" heading and the table. State next to the summary and audio: "This summary and audio are not part of the official statistics. The main points and data table are the official figures." Test which figures users believe are official after meeting only the first content.
items.impact: People with cognitive or learning disabilities, low numeracy, and screen-reader users reading in order are likely to take the label at face value and use the first or easiest format. They treat wrong, machine-made figures as official and quotable, and may repeat or act on them, for example in benefit, job or advocacy decisions.
items.problem: The page labels itself "Official statistics" at the top but does not say the AI summary and audio briefing fall outside that status, so they appear to carry it. Both give figures that differ from the release (F1, F2). Evidence: the status line sits directly above the AI section and nothing on the page limits its scope.
items.where:
bulletin.html, `

Official statistics. Released 11 November 2026...

` directly above `section.glance`, and the audio button below it
